title: National Sasquatch Awareness Day is a reminder of Bigfoot's local ties
excerpt: Annual day for Bigfoot lore marks the purported anniversary of the Patterson-Gimlin film's sasquatch encounter.
content:
National Sasquatch Awareness Day is Tuesday, marking the anniversary of the day Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin purported to encounter a large, bipedal creature loping through the Northern California woods in 1967 and captured the moment on nearly 60 seconds of film.

The Patterson-Gimlin film is arguably the most high-profile sasquatch "sighting" in U.S. history and inspired investigations by legions of Bigfoot believers - and skeptics - in the years following its release. Public fascination with the sasquatch has endured, and stories of Bigfoot encounters keep popping up across the country, from the deep forests of the Pacific Northwest to areas not too far from New York's Capital Region.

Related: Mysterious creatures shape New York folklore

In Washington County, the annual Sasquatch Festival and Calling Contest draws impressive crowds to the village of Whitehall each year for an event celebrating a multitude of local Bigfoot sightings dating back to the 1970s. The most recent festival, held Sept. 26, drew some of the event's largest crowds in its 10-year history.

Along with inspiring the 2016 film "The Beast of Whitehall," the community's relationship with Bigfoot led to the establishment of an official resolution declaring Whitehall a sasquatch sanctuary. Whitehall even made the sasquatch the village's "official animal" in 2018.

That welcoming environment could be why the Glens Falls metropolitan region - encompassing Warren and Washington counties, as categorized by the Census Bureau - currently sits in third place on a ranked list of the metro areas where you're most likely to spot a sasquatch. According to a report assembled by oddsmakers for Canada Sports Betting, the greater Glens Falls region ranks just below Grants Pass, Oregon, and Flagstaff, Arizona, when it comes to the number of sasquatch sightings per 100,000 residents.

That level of ubiquity in local lore isn't limited to just Whitehall and surrounding areas, either. Groups like Bigfoot Researchers of the Hudson Valley - based in Red Hook - have been investigating reports of sasquatch encounters around the region for years and remain active to this day.

And although it doesn't qualify as a true Bigfoot sighting, it wasn't that long ago that Albany itself was visited by Saxsquatch, the saxophone-playing sasquatch, in an uncharacteristically public - and musical - appearance for the famous cryptid.

That being the case, no matter which side of the belief spectrum one falls on, National Sasquatch Awareness Day offers an opportunity to acknowledge that Bigfoot is just as likely to call the Capital Region home as anywhere else in the nation.
